name: Cuttle
description: Cuttle is a 2-player card game where players use a standard 52-card deck as both resources and attacks. Each card can be played as a 'point card' (placed face-up contributing its rank to your score) or as an 'effect card' (using its special ability against the opponent). The goal is to accumulate 21 or more points in your tableau. Cuttle is one of the oldest card games still actively played in competitive circuits, with origins possibly dating to the 17th century.

history.origins: Cuttle's exact origins are unclear but it is believed to be an extremely old English card game, possibly dating to the 17th century. It gained a modern following through the online platform cuttle.cards which created a standardised ruleset and competitive scene.
timeline: 20th century: Documented in American card game books.
2010s-present: Revival via online competitive play at cuttle.cards.
history.cultural: One of the few ancient card games with a thriving modern competitive digital community.
history.evolution: The modern standardised ruleset clarified card abilities and made the game competitive. A growing online community now runs tournaments.

setup.dealing: 5 cards each. Remaining deck is the draw pile.
setup.equipment: 52-card deck. Play area for each player's tableau.

rules.objective: Be the first to have 21 or more points in your tableau (point cards face-up in front of you).
rules.gameplay: Draw 1 at turn start. Play card as point (face-up to your tableau) or effect (use its ability vs opponent). Kings lower win target by 7 each. Queens protect from Jack/scuttle. First to reach win target wins.
keyRules: Draw a card at the START of every turn (not optional).
Kings permanently lower the winning total: each King â†’ -7 from current threshold.
Queens protect your cards from being scuttled or Jacked.

strategy.basic: Build points with high-rank cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks as points). Use scuttles to destroy threats.
strategy.intermediate: Queen protection is crucial â€” a Queen in your tableau prevents Jacks and most scuttles from targeting your cards. Play Queens early.
strategy.advanced: King lowering strategy: with 3 Kings lowering the target to 7, the game ends very quickly. Pressure opponents who are building Queens with Jacks (steal) and Tens (clear effects). Eight (glasses) while opponent has a weak hand forces them to play suboptimally.
tips: A Queen in play protects all your other point cards from Jacks.
